Fixture 67: Coordinate Shapes (corner-shape family)

The 34 corner-shape properties · superellipse corners drawn inside the used border radius · Chrome 155 support badge per row · font-family "Liberation Sans"

COORDINATE-SHAPES

One live example per property. Each box keeps a 24px corner box, and the corner curve inside that box follows the CSS Borders 4 superellipse map. Rows 1-8 shape a single physical or logical corner on a 24px radius baseline; rows 9-16 shape a two-corner pair; row 17 uses the four-value corner-shape shorthand; rows 18-34 use the shorthands that set a radius and a shape together on a radiusless box. The engine turns each non-round corner into one outline path, so the fill and the solid border follow the same curve. The badge marks whether Chrome 155 ships the property: green means yes, red means the shorthand is in the draft but not implemented in Chrome yet.

round (K=1, initial)
scoop (K=-1)
bevel (K=0)
notch (K=-infinity)
square (K=+infinity)
squircle (K=2)
superellipse(2.5)

Shape longhands: one corner

Rows 1-8. Physical names and the logical twins on the fixed left-to-right map.

# Property / value What it does Effect (live)
1 corner-top-left-shape
shape longhand · physical corner · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Chamfers only the top-left corner box; the other three keep the round quarter-ellipse.
bevel: straight chamfer (K=0)
2 corner-top-right-shape
shape longhand · physical corner · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Scoops only the top-right corner box into a concave arc.
scoop: concave arc (K=-1)
3 corner-bottom-right-shape
shape longhand · physical corner · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Cuts the bottom-right corner box inward as a notch.
notch: concave V to the inner corner (K=-infinity)
4 corner-bottom-left-shape
shape longhand · physical corner · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Rounds the bottom-left corner box toward a squircle (flatter sides than a quarter-ellipse).
squircle: squared superellipse (K=2)
5 corner-start-start-shape
shape longhand · logical, fixed LTR map · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Logical start-start is top-left in horizontal left-to-right flow; same shape as row 1.
start-start = top-left
6 corner-start-end-shape
shape longhand · logical, fixed LTR map · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Logical start-end is top-right; same shape as row 2.
start-end = top-right
7 corner-end-start-shape
shape longhand · logical, fixed LTR map · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Logical end-start is bottom-left; same shape as row 4 shifted to the left edge.
end-start = bottom-left
8 corner-end-end-shape
shape longhand · logical, fixed LTR map · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Logical end-end is bottom-right; same shape as row 4.
end-end = bottom-right

Shape longhands: a two-corner pair

Rows 9-16. One value sets both corners of the pair; two values run left then right (top and bottom sides) or top then bottom (left and right sides).

# Property / value What it does Effect (live)
9 corner-top-shape
pair longhand · left then right · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Two values shape the top-left then the top-right corner; the bottom corners stay round.
bevel (left) then scoop (right)
10 corner-bottom-shape
pair longhand · left then right · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Two values shape the bottom-left then the bottom-right corner.
scoop (left) then bevel (right)
11 corner-left-shape
pair longhand · top then bottom · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Two values shape the top-left then the bottom-left corner.
notch (top) then scoop (bottom)
12 corner-right-shape
pair longhand · top then bottom · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Two values shape the top-right then the bottom-right corner.
squircle (top) then square (bottom)
13 corner-block-start-shape
pair longhand · logical, fixed LTR map · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Start then end on the inline axis: start-start then start-end, which is both top corners.
one value: both top corners notched
14 corner-block-end-shape
pair longhand · logical, fixed LTR map · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Start then end on the block-end side: both bottom corners.
one value: both bottom corners notched
15 corner-inline-start-shape
pair longhand · logical, fixed LTR map · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Start then end on the block axis: start-start then end-start, which is both left corners.
one value: both left corners notched
16 corner-inline-end-shape
pair longhand · logical, fixed LTR map · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Start then end on the inline-end side: both right corners.
one value: both right corners notched

corner-shape: the four-value shorthand

Row 17. Values shape the top-left, top-right, bottom-right, and bottom-left corners in border-radius order; missing values copy per border-radius.

# Property / value What it does Effect (live)
17 corner-shape
shorthand · 1 to 4 values · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		The four values shape the top-left, top-right, bottom-right, and bottom-left corners in that order, the border-radius path order; a missing bottom copies top, a missing right copies top, and a missing left copies right. Chrome 155 resolves the same declaration to the same four corner shapes.
top-left scoop, top-right bevel, bottom-right notch, bottom-left squircle

Radius-plus-shape shorthands

Rows 18-34. Each shorthand sets the corner radius and the shape together; a missing piece resets to its initial value. Chrome 155 does not implement these yet, so its column shows plain 0 or 24px radius corners for these rows.

# Property / value What it does Effect (live)

Chrome badges captured 2026-10-17 against Chrome 155.0.8059.84 with CSS.supports per property: the 16 shape longhands and corner-shape are supported with every keyword and both superellipse infinity forms; the 17 corner and corner-* shorthands are not implemented. Row 17's four-corner resolution was captured from the same build with getComputedStyle (corners resolve in border-radius order; missing values copy like border-radius). Named wave limits on the engine side: a non-round corner with a dashed or dotted border paints a solid path, border sides that differ in width or color keep the rounded stroke-rect geometry, background-clip and overflow clip keep their existing boxes instead of following the shaped outer path, and box-shadow keeps today's radii. Logical names use the fixed horizontal left-to-right map (no vertical writing-mode table yet).
